articles.title: What is GEO? A plain guide to AI search
articles.excerpt: Key takeaways GEO means making your content easy for AI answer tools to find, understand and cite. Google says optimising for its AI features is the same work as SEO, with no extra markup or files req…
articles.body: Key takeaways GEO means making your content easy for AI answer tools to find, understand and cite. Google says optimising for its AI features is the same work as SEO, with no extra markup or files required. The basics decide eligibility: pages must be crawlable, indexed and allowed to show a snippet. Be wary of anything sold as a secret: llms.txt, content chopped into fragments and tools claiming inside data have no support from Google. Measure with Search Console, your own analytics and a fixed list of real questions, and expect variation. What is GEO? GEO, short for generative engine optimisation, is the practice of making your content easy for AI answer tools to find, understand and cite.

articles.title: Neural Networks, its Inspiration and Various Components.
articles.excerpt: Introduction In this article we will walk through how one of these networks actually gets built and trained in code, using real screenshots from a working example. This is the network's structure, bui…
articles.body: Introduction In this week, I got introduced to Deep learning, and one key takeaway was on neural networks. I discovered that a neural network is a way of getting a computer to learn patterns from data the whole concept is loosely inspired by how the human brain works. For instancem in your brain, neurons receive signals, decide whether those signals are strong enough to matter, and pass a signal onward if they are. A neural network copies this idea in a much simpler mathematical form where a "neuron" takes in some numbers, combines them, and passes the result forward, layer by layer, until the network produces a final answer. In this article we will walk through how one of these networks actually gets built and trained in code, using real screenshots from a working example. 1.

articles.excerpt: Can AI truly be private?
articles.body: As artificial intelligence becomes an everyday essential, privacy has emerged as its greatest compromise. Mainstream platforms like ChatGPT and Google Gemini rely heavily on persistent user profiles, behavioral tracking, and vast datasets — often drawn directly from your prompts — to train their models. Enter DuckDuckGo AI Chat (accessible via Duck.ai ). Promoted as a privacy-first alternative, it promises access to leading AI models without corporate surveillance. It’s a tempting offer for sure. But is DuckDuckGo AI genuinely a better alternative to Gemini and ChatGPT , or does its focus on anonymity come at the cost of capability?

articles.body: Earlier this week, Marvel announced that it was discontinuing the Marvel Unlimited app , only to have it replaced by the new Marvel Comics app, powered by Webtoon. At New York Comic Con I had the chance to go hands-on with the app, and I am struggling to see why it needs to exist. Just like Marvel Unlimited, the new Marvel Comics app will bring the entire Marvel and Star Wars comics libraries at both of its subscription tiers. On the surface, the big advantage Webtoon has over Unlimited is how quickly new comics will be available — with the more expensive ‘Ultimate’ tier getting new issues 30 days after print, rather than Unlimited’s 90 day waiting period.

The initiatives are announced in conjunction with the White House Office of Science and Technology Policy’s (OSTP) “Science: A Golden Age Summit” in Washington on Thursday with top U.S. agency leaders.
